THE BP REGIME QUESTION, SHARPENED: Blomer-Pascadi Theorem 1.1 improves the per-v Kloosterman step when the bilateral length sits at the critical relation min(B,C) ~ v^{1/2}. Here v ~ V = N2/d and the bilateral variables are B, C with BC ~ U = N1/d and B, C >= W = U^{1/4}: at the BALANCED splitting rho = 1/2, U ~ V ~ N^{1/2}/d, so min(B,C) ~ U^{1/2} ~ V^{1/2} - the step IS critical for all d in the balanced regime (h ~ 1 in PRZZ). At UNBALANCED rho, U != V and only the sub-critical part improves. So the first line of the deep-read should confirm the actual rho used in PR's Conrey calculation (if rho = 1/2, a positive measure of v-steps is critical and the BP saving c^{-1/32} applies term-wise there; if rho != 1/2, the saving applies only on a restricted v-range and the net effect must be recomputed).
